items.followUp: What is the role of ATP in cellular activities?

rubric.why: Identifies ATP and its main biological role.
rubric.description: Names ATP and states that it is the cell’s energy currency.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for expanding ATP as adenosine triphosphate and identifying it as the energy currency of the cell.

rubric.why: Shows knowledge of the components of an ATP molecule.
rubric.description: States that ATP consists of adenine, ribose and three phosphate groups.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly naming the three components.

modelAnswer: ATP stands for adenosine triphosphate.
It is made up of adenine, ribose sugar and three phosphate groups.
ATP is the energy currency of the cell; energy is released when its terminal phosphate bond is broken.

items.followUp: Define an enzyme and state one way in which it speeds up a reaction.

rubric.why: Tests the meaning of an inhibitor.
rubric.description: Defines inhibitors as substances that decrease or stop enzyme activity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing their effect on enzyme activity.

rubric.why: Tests the meaning of an activator.
rubric.description: Defines activators as substances that increase enzyme activity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing their effect on enzyme activity.

modelAnswer: Inhibitors are substances that decrease or stop the activity of an enzyme.
Activators are substances that increase the activity of an enzyme.

items.followUp: What are enzymes? Give two examples of reactions in which they act as biocatalysts.

accept: increase the rate of biochemical reactions
rubric.why: Tests the definition of biocatalysts.
rubric.description: Defines biocatalysts as biological substances, usually enzymes, that speed up biochemical reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying them as biological catalysts or stating that they speed up biochemical reactions.

rubric.why: Tests benefits of using biocatalysts.
rubric.description: Gives two benefits, such as working under mild conditions, being highly specific, remaining unchanged after reactions, or lowering activation energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two correct benefits.

modelAnswer: Biocatalysts are biological catalysts, usually enzymes, that increase the rate of biochemical reactions.
They work efficiently under mild conditions in living cells.
They are highly specific and are not used up in the reactions they catalyse.

items.followUp: What is enzyme-substrate specificity? Give an example of an enzyme and its substrate.

rubric.why: Tests the meaning of enzyme specificity.
rubric.description: Explains that an enzyme acts on only a particular substrate or a limited range of substrates.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an enzyme is specific to its substrate.

rubric.why: Tests the application of specificity using a valid enzyme-substrate pair.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example of an enzyme and the substrate on which it acts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correctly matched enzyme and substrate.

modelAnswer: Enzyme specificity is the ability of an enzyme to act on a particular substrate because its active site fits that substrate.
For example, urease acts on urea.

items.followUp: What are microvilli, and how do they help in absorption?

rubric.why: Tests identification and location of villi.
rubric.description: Defines villi as finger-like projections of the lining of the small intestine.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing their shape and location.

rubric.why: Tests the function of villi.
rubric.description: States that villi increase surface area for absorption of digested food.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating their absorptive function.

modelAnswer: Villi are numerous finger-like projections of the lining of the small intestine.
They increase the surface area and help absorb digested nutrients into the blood and lymph.

items.followUp: Explain how biology is related to physics, chemistry, mathematics, geography and economics.

rubric.why: Tests the link between biology and physics.
rubric.description: Names biophysics and explains that it applies principles of physics to biological processes or structures.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct branch and its relevant connection to physics.

rubric.why: Tests the link between biology and chemistry.
rubric.description: Names biochemistry and explains that it studies the chemical substances and reactions of living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct branch and its relevant connection to chemistry.

rubric.why: Tests the link between biology and mathematics.
rubric.description: Names biometry or biomathematics and explains that mathematical methods are used to measure or analyse biological data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct branch and its relevant connection to mathematics.

rubric.why: Tests the link between biology and geography.
rubric.description: Names biogeography and explains that it studies the geographical distribution of organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct branch and its relevant connection to geography.

rubric.why: Tests the link between biology and economics.
rubric.description: Names bioeconomics and explains that it considers the economic use or value of biological resources.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct branch and its relevant connection to economics.

modelAnswer: Biology is related to physics through biophysics, which applies physical principles to living organisms and their processes.
Biology is related to chemistry through biochemistry, which studies the chemical substances and reactions in living organisms.
Biology is related to mathematics through biometry or biomathematics, which uses mathematical methods to measure and analyse biological data.
Biology is related to geography through biogeography, which studies the distribution of organisms in different regions.
Biology is related to economics through bioeconomics, which studies the economic use and value of biological resources.

items.followUp: Define exocytosis and distinguish it from endocytosis.

accept: movement of substances into the cell
rubric.why: Tests the definition and basic mechanism of endocytosis.
rubric.description: Defines endocytosis as the uptake of substances into a cell by inward folding of the plasma membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing cellular uptake and membrane invagination.

rubric.why: Tests how material is enclosed and the main forms of endocytosis.
rubric.description: States that the membrane encloses material in a vesicle and/or correctly describes phagocytosis or pinocytosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct vesicle description or a correct type with what it takes in.

rubric.why: The question asks for a labelled diagram of endocytosis.
rubric.description: Provides a diagram showing membrane folding around an external particle and forming an internal vesicle, with appropriate labels.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a recognisable labelled diagram showing the process and at least three relevant labels.

rubric.why: Checks understanding of the two commonly described forms of endocytosis.
rubric.description: Correctly distinguishes phagocytosis (solid particles) from pinocytosis (liquids).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating both forms and what each takes in.

modelAnswer: Endocytosis is the process by which a cell takes in substances from outside by folding its plasma membrane inward.
The membrane surrounds the substance and pinches off inside the cell to form a vesicle.
Phagocytosis is the uptake of solid particles; pinocytosis is the uptake of liquids.

Diagram construction: draw and label an external particle beside the cell; draw the cell membrane folding inward around it; show the membrane edges joining to enclose the particle in a vesicle inside the cytoplasm.
Labels: external particle; plasma membrane; inward fold; vesicle; cytoplasm.

items.followUp: Define endangered species and name three threatened animal species found in Pakistan.

rubric.why: Tests the definition of extinct.
rubric.description: Defines an extinct species as one that has no living members remaining anywhere.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the species no longer exists or has no living members.

rubric.why: Tests the meaning of endangered species.
rubric.description: Explains that endangered species face a serious risk of extinction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the risk of extinction.

rubric.why: Tests knowledge of endangered or threatened wildlife in Pakistan.
rubric.description: Names examples of threatened or endangered animal species found in Pakistan.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark each for two correct examples, up to 2 marks.

rubric.why: Tests an explanation of why these species are threatened or how they can be protected.
rubric.description: Gives a relevant threat or conservation measure, such as habitat loss, hunting or establishing protected areas.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid cause of endangerment or one appropriate conservation measure.

modelAnswer: A species is extinct when no living members of it remain anywhere in the world.
An endangered species is one that is at serious risk of becoming extinct.
Threatened wildlife in Pakistan includes the Indus river dolphin, snow leopard, houbara bustard and green sea turtle.
Habitat destruction, hunting and pollution can reduce their populations.
Protecting habitats and preventing illegal hunting help conserve these species.
